title: The First Letter to the Corinthians
lead: Paul's long letter from Ephesus (about AD 53-55) to the church he founded in Corinth. It answers a report of quarrels and a letter of questions, and it covers divisions, sexual conduct, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, worship, spiritual gifts, love and the resurrection.

sections.h: Chapters 1-4: a church divided over teachers
sections.b: Paul answers the news that the Corinthians are saying "I belong to Paul" or "I belong to Apollos". His reply sets the cross of Christ against human wisdom and boasting: God chose what is weak and foolish by the world's measure (1:18-31); the Spirit gives the wisdom of God (2:6-16); and all teachers are servants and stewards, not masters (3:5-9; 4:1-5). He ends as a father who may have to come with a rod (4:14-21).
